Additional Operation Response Parameters: RFC 7644 SCIM Protocol Specification September 2015 Clients MAY request a partial resource representation on any operation that returns a resource within the response by specifying either of the mutually exclusive URL query parameters "attributes" or "excludedAttributes", as follows: attributes When specified, the default list of attributes SHALL be overridden, and each resource returned MUST contain the minimum set of resource attributes and any attributes or sub-attributes explicitly requested by the "attributes" parameter. The query parameter attributes value is a comma-separated list of resource attribute names in standard attribute notation ( Section 3.10 ) form (e.g., userName, name, emails). excludedAttributes When specified, each resource returned MUST contain the minimum set of resource attributes. Additionally, the default set of attributes minus those attributes listed in "excludedAttributes" is returned. The query parameter attributes value is a comma-separated list of resource attribute names in standard attribute notation ( Section 3.10 ) form (e.g., userName, name, emails). GET /Users/2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646?attributes=userName Host: example.com Accept: application/scim+json Authorization: Bearer h480djs93hd8 The following response is returned: HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: application/scim+json Location: https://example.com/v2/Users/2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646 ETag: W/"a330bc54f0671c9" { "schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"], "id":"2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646", "userName":"bjensen" } Hunt, et al. Standards Track [Page 65] RFC 7644 SCIM Protocol Specification September 2015 3.10 . Attribute Notation All operations share a common scheme for referencing simple and complex attributes. In general, attributes are uniquely identified by prefixing the attribute name with its schema URN separated by a colon (":") character; e.g., the core User resource attribute 'userName' is identified as "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User:userName". Clients MAY omit core schema attribute URN prefixes but SHOULD fully qualify extended attributes with the associated schema extension URN to avoid naming conflicts. For example, the attribute 'age' defined in "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:exampleCo:2.0:hr" is uniquely identified as "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:exampleCo:2.0:hr:age". Complex attributes' sub-attributes are referenced via nested dot ('.') notation, i.e., {urn}:{Attribute name}.{Sub-Attribute name}. For example, the fully qualified path for a User's givenName is "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User:name.givenName". All facets (URN, attribute, and sub-attribute name) of the fully encoded attribute name are case insensitive. 3.11 . "/Me" Authenticated Subject Alias A client MAY use a URL of the form "<base-URI>/Me" as a URI alias for the User or other resource associated with the currently authenticated subject for any SCIM operation. A service provider MAY respond in one of three ways: o A service provider that does NOT support this feature SHOULD respond with HTTP status code 501 (Not Implemented). o A service provider MAY choose to redirect the client using HTTP status code 308 (Permanent Redirect) to the resource associated with the authenticated subject. The client MAY then repeat the request at the indicated location. o A service provider MAY process the SCIM request directly. In any response, the HTTP "Location" header MUST be the permanent location of the aliased resource associated with the authenticated subject. When using the SCIM Create Resource command (HTTP POST) with the "/Me" alias, the desired resourceType being created is at the discretion of the service provider, based on the authenticated subject (if not anonymous) making the request and any request body attributes (e.g., "schemas"). See Section 7.6 for information on security considerations related to this operation. Hunt, et al. Standards Track

Versioning Resources: RFC 7644 SCIM Protocol Specification September 2015 Example create request: POST /Users HTTP/1.1 Host: example.com Content-Type: application/scim+json Authorization: Bearer h480djs93hd8 Content-Length: ... { "schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"], "userName":"bjensen", "externalId":"bjensen", "name":{ "formatted":"Ms. Barbara J Jensen III", "familyName":"Jensen", "givenName":"Barbara" } } The server responds with an ETag in the response header and meta structure: HTTP/1.1 201 Created Content-Type: application/scim+json Location: https://example.com/v2/Users/2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646 ETag: W/"e180ee84f0671b1" { "schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"], "id":"2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646", "meta":{ "resourceType":"User", "created":"2011-08-01T21:32:44.882Z", "lastModified":"2011-08-01T21:32:44.882Z", "location": "https://example.com/v2/Users/2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646", "version":"W\/\"e180ee84f0671b1\"" }, "name":{ "formatted":"Ms. Barbara J Jensen III", "familyName":"Jensen", "givenName":"Barbara" }, "userName":"bjensen" } Hunt, et al. An example of conditional retrieval, using the If-None-Match header ( Section 3.2 of [RFC7232] ): GET /Users/2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646?attributes=displayName Host: example.com Accept: application/scim+json Authorization: Bearer h480djs93hd8 If-None-Match: W/"e180ee84f0671b1" If the resource has not changed, the service provider simply returns an empty body with a 304 (Not Modified) response code. Service Provider Configuration Endpoints SCIM defines three endpoints to facilitate discovery of SCIM service provider features and schema that MAY be retrieved using HTTP GET: /ServiceProviderConfig An HTTP GET to this endpoint will return a JSON structure that describes the SCIM specification features available on a service provider. This endpoint SHALL return responses with a JSON object using a "schemas" attribute of "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:ServiceProviderConfig". The attributes returned in the JSON object are defined in Section 5 of [RFC7643] . An example representation of SCIM service provider configuration may be found in Section 8.5 of [RFC7643] . Hunt, et al. Standards Track [Page 73]

Service Provider Configuration Endpoints: RFC 7644 SCIM Protocol Specification September 2015 /Schemas An HTTP GET to this endpoint is used to retrieve information about resource schemas supported by a SCIM service provider. An HTTP GET to the endpoint "/Schemas" SHALL return all supported schemas in ListResponse format (see Figure 3). Individual schema definitions can be returned by appending the schema URI to the /Schemas endpoint. For example: /Schemas/urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User The contents of each schema returned are described in Section 7 of [RFC7643] . An example representation of SCIM schemas may be found in Section 8.7 of [RFC7643] . /ResourceTypes An HTTP GET to this endpoint is used to discover the types of resources available on a SCIM service provider (e.g., Users and Groups). Each resource type defines the endpoints, the core schema URI that defines the resource, and any supported schema extensions. The attributes defining a resource type can be found in Section 6 of [RFC7643] , and an example representation can be found in Section 8.6 of [RFC7643] . In cases where a request is for a specific "ResourceType" or "Schema", the single JSON object is returned in the same way that a single User or Group is retrieved, as per Section 3.4.1 . When returning multiple ResourceTypes or Schemas, the message form described by the "urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:ListResponse" (ListResponse) form SHALL be used as shown in Figure 3 and in Figure 9 below. Query parameters described in Section 3.4.2 , such as filtering, sorting, and pagination, SHALL be ignored. If a "filter" is provided, the service provider SHOULD respond with HTTP status code 403 (Forbidden) to ensure that clients cannot incorrectly assume that any matching conditions specified in a filter are true. Hunt, et al. Multi-Tenancy: RFC 7644 SCIM Protocol Specification September 2015 The SCIM protocol does not prescribe the mechanisms whereby clients and service providers interact for the following: o Registering or provisioning Tenants o Associating a subset of clients with a subset of the Tenants o Indicating which tenant is associated with the data in a request or response, or indicating which Tenant is the subject of a query 6.1 . Associating Clients to Tenants The service provider MAY use one of the authentication mechanisms discussed in Section 2 to determine the identity of the client and thus infer the associated Tenant. For implementations where a client is associated with more than one Tenant, the service provider MAY use one of the three methods below for explicit specification of the Tenant. If any of these methods of allowing the client to explicitly specify the Tenant are employed, the service provider should ensure that access controls are in place to prevent or allow cross-tenant use cases. The service provider should consider precedence in cases where a client may explicitly specify a Tenant while being implicitly associated with a different Tenant. In all of these methods, the {tenant_id} is a unique identifier for the Tenant as defined by the service provider. o A URL prefix: "https://www.example.com/Tenants/{tenant_id}/v2/ Users". o A sub-domain: "https://{tenant_id}.example.com/v2/Groups". o An HTTP header: The service provider may recognize a {tenant_id} provided by the client in an HTTP header as the indicator of the desired target Tenant. SCIM Identifiers with Multiple Tenants Considerations for a multi-tenant implementation: o The service provider may choose to implement SCIM ids that are unique across all resources for all Tenants, but this is not required. o The externalId, defined by the client, is required to be unique ONLY within the resources associated with the associated Tenant. 7 . Security Considerations 7.1 . HTTP Considerations The SCIM protocol layers on top of HTTP and is thus subject to the security considerations of HTTP ( Section 9 of [RFC7230] ) and its related specifications. As stated in Section 2.7.1 of [RFC7230] , a SCIM client MUST NOT generate the "userinfo" (i.e., username and password) component (and its "@" delimiter) when an "http" URI reference is generated with a message, as userinfo and its "@" delimiter are now disallowed in HTTP. 7.2 . TLS Support Considerations SCIM resources (e.g., Users and Groups) contain sensitive information, including passwords. Therefore, SCIM clients and service providers MUST require the use of a transport-layer security mechanism when communicating with SCIM service providers. The SCIM service provider MUST support TLS 1.2 [ RFC5246 ] and MAY support additional transport-layer mechanisms meeting its security requirements. When using TLS, the client MUST perform a TLS/SSL server identity check, per [ RFC6125 ]. Implementation security considerations for TLS can be found in [ RFC7525 ]. 7.3 . Authorization Token Considerations When using authorization tokens such as those issued by OAuth 2.0 [ RFC6749 ], implementers MUST take into account threats and countermeasures as documented in Section 8 of [RFC7521] . Hunt, et al. Standards Track [Page 78]

Bearer Token and Cookie Considerations Since the possession of a bearer token or cookie MAY authorize the holder to potentially read, modify, or delete resources, bearer tokens and cookies MUST contain sufficient entropy to prevent a random guessing attack; for example, see Section 5.2 of [RFC6750] and Section 5.1.4.2.2 of [RFC6819] . As with all SCIM communications, bearer tokens and HTTP cookies MUST be exchanged using TLS. Bearer tokens MUST have a limited lifetime that can be determined directly or indirectly (e.g., by checking with a validation service) by the service provider. By expiring tokens, clients are forced to obtain a new token (which usually involves re-authentication) for continued authorized access. For example, in OAuth 2.0, a client MAY use OAuth token refresh to obtain a new bearer token after authenticating to an authorization server. See Section 6 of [RFC6749] . As with bearer tokens, an HTTP cookie SHOULD last no longer than the lifetime of a browser session. An expiry time should be set that limits session cookie lifetime as per Section 5.2.1 of [RFC6265] . Implementations supporting OAuth bearer tokens need to factor in security considerations of this authorization method [ RFC7521 ]. Since security is only as good as the weakest link, implementers also need to consider authentication choices coupled with OAuth bearer tokens. The security considerations of the default authentication method for OAuth bearer tokens, HTTP Basic, are well documented in [ HTTP-BASIC-AUTH ]; therefore, implementers are encouraged to use stronger authentication methods. Designating the specific methods of authentication and authorization is out of scope for SCIM; however, this information is provided as a resource to implementers. 7.5 . Privacy Considerations 7.5.1 . Personal Information The SCIM Core Schema specification [ RFC7643 ] defines attributes that may contain personally identifying information as well as other sensitive personal data. The privacy considerations in the Security Considerations section of [ RFC7643 ] MUST be considered. Hunt, et al. Standards Track [Page 79]

ti: RFC 7644: SCIM Protocol
x: 7.5 . Privacy Considerations: RFC 7644 SCIM Protocol Specification September 2015 7.5.2 . Disclosure of Sensitive Information in URIs As mentioned in Section 9.4 of [RFC7231] , SCIM clients requesting information using query filters that use HTTP GET SHOULD give consideration to the information content of the filters and whether or not their exposure in a URI would represent a breach of security or confidentiality through leakage in web browsers or server logs. This is particularly true for information that is legally considered "personally identifiable information" or is otherwise restricted by privacy laws. In these situations, to ensure maximum security and confidentiality, clients SHOULD query using HTTP POST (see Section 3.4.3 ). Servers that receive HTTP GET requests using filters that contain sensitive or confidential personal information SHOULD respond with HTTP status code 403 to indicate that the operation is forbidden. A "scimType" error code of "sensitive" may be returned to indicate that the request must be submitted using POST. The following is a non-normative example: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden { "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"], "detail": "Query filter involving 'name' is restricted or confidential", "scimType": "sensitive", "status": "404" } 7.6 . Anonymous Requests If a SCIM service provider accepts anonymous requests such as SCIM resource creation requests (via HTTP POST), appropriate security measures should be put in place to prevent or limit exposure to attacks. The following countermeasures MAY be used: o Try to authenticate web user interface components that formulate the SCIM creation request. While the end-user may be anonymous, the web user interface component often has its own way to authenticate to the SCIM service provider (e.g., has an OAuth client credential [ RFC6749 ]), and the web user interface component may implement its own measures (e.g., the Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart (CAPTCHA)) to ensure that a legitimate request is being made. o Limit the number of requests that any particular client MAY make in a period of time. Hunt, et al. Standards Track [Page 80]

ti: RFC 7644: SCIM Protocol
x: 7.6 . Anonymous Requests: RFC 7644 SCIM Protocol Specification September 2015 o For User resources, default newly created resources with an "active" setting of "false", and use a secondary confirmation process (e.g., email confirmation) to ensure that the resource created is real. 7.7 . Secure Storage and Handling of Sensitive Data An attacker may obtain valid username/password combinations from the SCIM service provider's underlying database by gaining access to the database and/or launching injection attacks. This could lead to unintended disclosure of username/password combinations. The impact may extend beyond the domain of the SCIM service provider if the data was provisioned from other domains. Administrators should undertake industry best practices to protect the storage of credentials and, in particular, SHOULD follow recommendations outlined in Section 5.1.4.1 of [RFC6819] . These recommendations include, but are not limited to, the following: o Provide injection attack countermeasures (e.g., by validating all inputs and parameters); o Credentials should not be stored in cleartext form; o Store credentials using an encrypted protection mechanism (e.g., hashing); and o Where possible, avoid passwords as the sole form of authentication, and consider using credentials that are based on asymmetric cryptography. As outlined in Section 5.1.4.2 of [RFC6819] , administrators SHOULD take countermeasures such as the following, to prevent online attacks on secrets: o Utilize a secure password policy in order to increase user password entropy, which will in turn hinder online attacks and password guessing; o Mitigate attacks on passwords by locking respective accounts that have a number of failed attempts; o Use "tar pit" techniques by temporarily locking a respective account and delaying responses for a certain duration. The duration may increase with the number of failed attempts; and Hunt, et al. Standards Track [Page 81]

Secure Storage and Handling of Sensitive Data: RFC 7644 SCIM Protocol Specification September 2015 o Use authentication systems that use CAPTCHAs and other factors for authenticating users, to further reduce the possibility of automated attacks. Service providers SHOULD define an access control model that differentiates between individual client applications and their specific need to access information, and any User self-service rights to review and update personal profile information. This may include OAuth 2.0 delegation profiles that allow client systems to act on behalf of users with their permission. 7.8 . ti: Okta Businesses at Work report
x: Frequently asked questions: Identity security is critical because agentic AI operates at machine scale, where human bottlenecks can quickly become security backdoors. As organizations deploy autonomous agents, “agentic AI readiness is identity readiness”—meaning success depends on a unified identity fabric that governs both human and non-human identities to prevent unauthorized access or “shadow AI” risks. While enterprise enthusiasm is high, adoption is widespread but still “measured” and “cautious”. The vast majority of businesses—82% combined—report their AI agent usage as either “moderate” or “limited”. Leaders are moving deliberately to address identity, governance, and compliance risks before moving these autonomous systems into full-scale production. According to the 2026 report, being ready for AI agents is actually about being ready for identity security. To stay ahead, companies must move toward implementing an “identity security fabric”. This bridges the gaps in how they handle logins, permissions, and automated account oversight so that their security system works seamlessly for both people and software-driven identities. The main hurdles aren’t what the AI can do, but how it is governed. 58% of leaders worry most about identity management and access risks. Furthermore, 78% of organizations struggle with managing “non-human” identities—like the service accounts AI uses—and a staggering 90% of companies still don’t have a clear plan to secure them. As AI agents introduce continuous access changes, manual approvals have transformed from simple administrative tasks into major security risks. Access requests and certifications have surged more than 8-11x over the past two years, making it nearly impossible for humans to keep pace with the velocity of agentic workflows without automated governance. The volume of detected threats is “exploding”, particularly in sectors with historically less robust identity infrastructure. Nonprofits saw their threat-to-authentication ratio soar to 78% this year, up from 18% the previous year. Wholesale trade ranks second with a 44% ratio. Energy, mining, oil, and gas follows at 29%.

x: Automate Joiner/Mover/Leaver for a test tenant: create users from CSV, assign groups by department, disable and strip access on leave, log every change. Get a free Microsoft 365 developer/trial tenant (or use Entra free tier) Install Microsoft.Graph PowerShell; connect with least-privilege scopes Write New-Joiner.ps1 reading users.csv → New-MgUser + group membership by dept Write Move-User.ps1 swapping groups on dept change Write Remove-Leaver.ps1: disable, revoke sessions, remove groups, export audit CSV Add -WhatIf support and a log file Push to your own GitHub repo with README and sample CSV (fake data only)

ti: Entra Conditional Access baseline
x: Design and document a Conditional Access baseline: MFA for all, block legacy auth, admin protections, device compliance, break-glass accounts. Create 2 break-glass accounts excluded from all policies Build policies in report-only mode first Require MFA for admins; then all users Block legacy authentication Require compliant device for sensitive apps (doc if no Intune) Use What If tool and sign-in logs to validate Export policies as JSON (Graph) into your repo

ti: PIM + access reviews
x: Show privileged access done right: just-in-time admin roles, approval, and recurring access reviews. Enable Entra ID P2 trial Make Global/User Admin roles eligible (not active) in PIM Require MFA + justification + approval on activation Set max activation 4 hours; enable alerts Create quarterly access review for privileged roles and a group Complete a review; document outcomes

ti: Okta SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning demo
x: Connect a SaaS/test app to Okta with SAML SSO and SCIM automatic provisioning. Sign up for a free Okta Integrator (developer) org Add a SAML app (e.g., a SAML test SP) and configure ACS/Entity ID Assign users/groups; test SP- and IdP-initiated login Capture a SAML assertion with SAML-tracer and annotate it Enable SCIM to an app that supports it (or a SCIM test server) and show create/deactivate Document the flow with a diagram

ti: IAM audit report script
x: One script that produces an access hygiene report: stale accounts, users without MFA, guests, privileged role holders, apps with expiring secrets. ti: SC-300: You are the identity administrator for Contoso. The company is planning a hybrid identity
x: You are the identity administrator for Contoso. The company is planning a hybrid identity solution and wants to minimize on-premises footprint while still synchronizing user accounts, groups, and password hashes to Microsoft Entra ID. Which synchronization method should you recommend? Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is the recommended lightweight agent-based solution that runs on multiple servers, has a smaller on-premises footprint, and supports synchronizing users, groups, and password hashes. Entra Connect is the older, heavier solution that requires more infrastructure. Pass-through authentication does not synchronize password hashes, and MIM is legacy and not the strategic direction.

ti: SC-300: Contoso uses Microsoft Entra Connect to synchronize identities. The on-premises Active Dir
x: Contoso uses Microsoft Entra Connect to synchronize identities. The on-premises Active Directory contains a security group named SG-Exec that should be synchronized to Entra ID as a Microsoft 365 Group with dynamic membership rules applied in the cloud. What must be done to achieve this? Security groups synchronized from on-premises cannot be directly converted to Microsoft 365 Groups with dynamic membership in Entra ID. The recommended approach is to enable group writeback and create a new dynamic Microsoft 365 Group in the cloud. Changing group type after sync is not supported, and switching sync tools does not solve the group type limitation.

ti: SC-300: Which of the following objects can be synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID using Entra Conne
x: Which of the following objects can be synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID using Entra Connect Cloud Sync? (Choose all that apply, but select the best single answer that represents the most complete option) Entra Cloud Sync supports synchronizing users, groups (security and Microsoft 365), and password hashes. It does not support device synchronization or public folder contacts (those require full Entra Connect). Option D is the most accurate single choice among the provided options.

ti: SC-300: You need to create a guest user account for a partner company that uses a non-Azure AD ide
x: You need to create a guest user account for a partner company that uses a non-Azure AD identity provider. The partner must be able to access a specific SharePoint Online site using their existing corporate credentials. What should you configure? Direct federation (SAML/WS-Fed) allows the partner to use their own corporate identity provider for authentication, which matches the requirement. Email OTP is for organizations without an identity provider. Google federation is limited to Google accounts only. Self-service sign-up is for consumer scenarios, not corporate partners.

ti: SC-300: What is the default synchronization interval for password hash synchronization when using
x: What is the default synchronization interval for password hash synchronization when using Microsoft Entra Connect? Password hash synchronization with Entra Connect occurs every 30 minutes by default. The 2-minute interval applies to other attribute syncs in newer versions, but password hash sync remains on a 30-minute cycle. The 2-hour and 24-hour options are incorrect.

ti: SC-300: Your organization has a requirement to prevent all guest users from being able to enumerat
x: Your organization has a requirement to prevent all guest users from being able to enumerate the membership of any Microsoft 365 Group. Which setting in the Microsoft Entra admin center should you modify? The Group settings option 'Restrict guest access to groups' controls whether guests can see group membership. This is the specific control needed. External collaboration settings control invitation and user access levels but do not directly control group membership visibility. The other options are unrelated.

ti: SC-300: You are configuring Microsoft Entra Connect for a hybrid environment. The company wants to
x: You are configuring Microsoft Entra Connect for a hybrid environment. The company wants to use Seamless Single Sign-On (SSO) and Password Hash Synchronization. Which two prerequisites must be met? (Choose two, but select the option that lists the correct pair) For Seamless SSO and PHS, the forest functional level must be at least Windows Server 2012 and the Entra Connect server must be domain joined. Option B is partially correct but incomplete. Option A is incorrect because the server does not require direct internet access if a proxy is configured. Option D is not required.

ti: SC-300: A user object synchronized from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID has the
x: A user object synchronized from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID has the attribute userType set to 'Member'. You want this user to be treated as a guest in Entra ID for licensing and Conditional Access purposes. What is the recommended way to achieve this? For synchronized users, the userType attribute is authoritative from on-premises and cannot be changed directly in Entra ID. The recommended and supported method is to update the userType using Microsoft Graph API (or PowerShell) in the cloud. Changing it on-premises is not honored for this attribute. The other options do not change the userType property.

ti: SC-300: Which of the following is a key advantage of Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync over Microsoft Ent
x: Which of the following is a key advantage of Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync over Microsoft Entra Connect? Entra Cloud Sync uses multiple lightweight agents for high availability and has a much smaller on-premises footprint than the full Entra Connect synchronization service. It does not support more object types (actually supports fewer), is not real-time, and still requires configuration for group writeback.

ti: SC-300: You manage external identities for Fabrikam. Several vendors need to access internal appli
x: You manage external identities for Fabrikam. Several vendors need to access internal applications using their own corporate identities from identity providers that support OpenID Connect. What feature should you configure in Microsoft Entra ID to meet this requirement with the least administrative effort? Microsoft Entra B2B direct federation supports both SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect identity providers, allowing users to sign in with their corporate credentials. This is the correct B2B feature for organizational partners. B2C is for consumer-facing applications, self-service sign-up is for email-based scenarios, and the SAML option is too narrow.

ti: SC-300: You are the identity administrator for Contoso. The company wants to synchronize user acco
x: You are the identity administrator for Contoso. The company wants to synchronize user accounts and groups from an on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID while minimizing the amount of data sent to the cloud. Which hybrid identity solution should you implement? Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is the recommended lightweight solution that uses a cloud-based provisioning agent and sends significantly less data to the cloud compared to the full Entra Connect sync client. Option A uses the legacy heavier client, option C is an authentication method not a sync method, and option D is a monitoring tool.

ti: SC-300: Which of the following objects can be synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID using Microsoft E
x: Which of the following objects can be synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID using Microsoft Entra Connect? Entra Connect can synchronize users, groups (both security and distribution), contacts, and devices. Option A is missing contacts, option C is too restrictive, and option D incorrectly limits group types and includes computer accounts which are not directly synced as objects.

ti: SC-300: Contoso is planning a merger with Fabrikam. Fabrikam users need to access Contoso resource
x: Contoso is planning a merger with Fabrikam. Fabrikam users need to access Contoso resources using their existing Fabrikam credentials without creating new accounts. What should you configure in Microsoft Entra ID? B2B collaboration allows external users (Fabrikam) to use their own credentials to access Contoso resources through invitations or self-service sign-up. Cross-tenant sync is for internal employee synchronization between tenants, not guest access. Options A and D are not the correct approach for this scenario.

ti: SC-300: You need to create a group in Microsoft Entra ID that will be used to assign licenses to u
x: You need to create a group in Microsoft Entra ID that will be used to assign licenses to users in the Marketing department. The group must be dynamically updated when users change departments. Which group type and membership type should you configure? A security group with dynamic user membership uses membership rules based on user attributes (such as department) and can be used for license assignment. Microsoft 365 groups can also be dynamic but are primarily for collaboration. Device membership is not applicable for user licensing.

ti: SC-300: Which protocol and port combination is used by default for synchronization between Microso
x: Which protocol and port combination is used by default for synchronization between Microsoft Entra Connect and Microsoft Entra ID? Microsoft Entra Connect uses outbound HTTPS connections over port 443 to communicate with Entra ID. LDAP, HTTP, and SMB are not used for the synchronization service communication with the cloud.

ti: SC-300: Your organization has a requirement to allow users to sign in with their on-premises crede
x: Your organization has a requirement to allow users to sign in with their on-premises credentials without storing password hashes in the cloud. Which authentication method should be implemented with Microsoft Entra Connect? Pass-through authentication validates passwords against on-premises Active Directory without storing hashes in the cloud. Password hash sync stores hashes, federation uses AD FS, and seamless SSO is a sign-in enhancement that works with either PHS or PTA.

ti: SC-300: You are configuring a new Entra ID tenant for a partner organization. You want to allow us
x: You are configuring a new Entra ID tenant for a partner organization. You want to allow users from contoso.com to access your applications as guests. What must be configured in the External Identities section? Cross-tenant access settings must be configured to allow inbound B2B access from specific tenants such as contoso.com. Adding as an identity provider is not required for standard B2B. B2C is for consumer identities, and conditional access is applied after the external user is allowed.

ti: SC-300: What is the maximum number of on-premises Active Directory forests that a single Microsoft
x: What is the maximum number of on-premises Active Directory forests that a single Microsoft Entra Connect server can synchronize to a single Microsoft Entra tenant? A single Entra Connect server can synchronize up to 5 on-premises AD forests to one Entra tenant. Synchronization from more than 5 forests requires additional Connect servers or the use of Entra Cloud Sync.

ti: SC-300: Litware Inc. wants to create a dynamic security group that includes all users whose job ti
x: Litware Inc. wants to create a dynamic security group that includes all users whose job title contains 'Manager' and who are located in the United States. Which membership rule syntax should be used? The correct syntax uses the -contains and -eq operators with the proper attribute names (jobTitle and country). Option B uses incorrect operator names, option C uses usageLocation instead of country and incorrect operators, and option D uses 'or' instead of 'and' and the wrong attribute (title).

ti: SC-300: You have deployed Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync for a hybrid environment. After the initial s
x: You have deployed Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync for a hybrid environment. After the initial sync cycle, you notice that several on-premises groups are missing in Entra ID. What is the most likely reason? The Cloud Sync service account requires the 'Replicating Directory Changes' permission on the on-premises domain to read group objects. Cloud Sync does support group synchronization (eliminating B), distribution groups are supported, and member count is not a limiting factor for visibility.

ti: SC-300: Your organization is planning to synchronize user accounts from an on-premises Active Dire
x: Your organization is planning to synchronize user accounts from an on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID. You need to choose a synchronization method that supports password hash synchronization, pass-through authentication, and seamless single sign-on while minimizing the number of servers required. Which solution should you recommend? Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is the recommended modern solution as it is a lightweight agent-based service that supports password hash sync, PTA, and SSO with significantly lower infrastructure requirements than the legacy Entra Connect sync client. Option A and C refer to the older Entra Connect sync client which requires more servers and maintenance. Option D is not a valid product name.

ti: SC-300: You are configuring group writeback from Microsoft Entra ID to an on-premises Active Direc
x: You are configuring group writeback from Microsoft Entra ID to an on-premises Active Directory. Which type of group can be successfully written back using Entra Connect? Only security groups that have assigned membership can be written back to on-premises AD. Microsoft 365 groups and dynamic groups are cloud-only and cannot be written back. This limitation is important when planning group management in hybrid environments.

ti: SC-300: Contoso is using Microsoft Entra Connect to synchronize identities. The HR department has
x: Contoso is using Microsoft Entra Connect to synchronize identities. The HR department has asked that all users with the job title 'Contractor' be automatically added to a specific security group in Microsoft Entra ID. What is the best way to achieve this requirement? Dynamic user groups in Microsoft Entra ID can automatically add or remove members based on attributes such as jobTitle. This is the most efficient method. Entra Connect OU filtering controls which objects are synchronized but does not create dynamic group membership in the cloud. Group writeback works in the opposite direction.

ti: SC-300: Which of the following is a valid source of authority for a user account that has been syn
x: Which of the following is a valid source of authority for a user account that has been synchronized from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID using Entra Connect? When an object is synchronized from on-premises AD using Entra Connect, the source of authority remains on-premises. Most attributes can only be changed in the on-premises AD and then synchronized to the cloud. This is a core concept of hybrid identity with Entra Connect.

ti: SC-300: You need to allow users from a partner organization using their own Azure AD tenant to acc
x: You need to allow users from a partner organization using their own Azure AD tenant to access your company's SaaS application registered in Microsoft Entra ID. What should you configure? Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration is designed for inviting and managing external users from other organizations (including other Azure AD tenants) to access your resources. B2C is for consumer-facing applications with local accounts or social identity providers. Domain Services is for managed domain services.

ti: SC-300: Your company is migrating from Microsoft Entra Connect to Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync. What
x: Your company is migrating from Microsoft Entra Connect to Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync. What is one key advantage of Cloud Sync over the traditional Entra Connect sync client? Entra Cloud Sync uses multiple lightweight provisioning agents that can be installed on several servers, providing high availability and eliminating the single point of failure that exists with the traditional Entra Connect sync client. Both solutions support large object counts and PHS.

ti: SC-300: What is the default synchronization interval when using Microsoft Entra Connect to sync ch
x: What is the default synchronization interval when using Microsoft Entra Connect to sync changes from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID? The default synchronization cycle for Entra Connect is every 30 minutes. While you can force a sync or change the schedule, the out-of-the-box setting is 30 minutes. Real-time synchronization is not available with Entra Connect.

ti: SC-300: You are the identity administrator for Fabrikam. The company has recently acquired a start
x: You are the identity administrator for Fabrikam. The company has recently acquired a startup that uses Google Workspace. Fabrikam wants these external users to access internal resources using their Google accounts. What is the recommended approach? Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration natively supports Google as an identity provider, allowing external users to sign in with their Google accounts without creating new credentials. This is the simplest and most secure approach for partner users. B2C is intended for consumer applications, not internal resource access.

ti: SC-300: Which attribute is used by default to match on-premises AD users with Microsoft Entra ID a
x: Which attribute is used by default to match on-premises AD users with Microsoft Entra ID accounts during the synchronization process with Entra Connect? By default, Entra Connect uses the msDS-ConsistencyGuid attribute (which is populated with the objectGUID value) as the source anchor for matching objects. This provides more flexibility than using objectGUID directly because it can be moved between forests. UPN and mail are used for sign-in but not as the immutable source anchor.

ti: SC-300: A company wants to implement a hybrid identity solution with the least possible on-premise
x: A company wants to implement a hybrid identity solution with the least possible on-premises footprint. They need to support password hash synchronization and self-service password reset writeback. Which deployment model meets these requirements? Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is specifically designed for organizations wanting a minimal on-premises footprint. It runs as a lightweight agent, supports password hash synchronization, and enables password writeback for self-service password reset. It is the strategic future direction from Microsoft.

ti: SC-300: You need to enforce MFA for all users accessing Microsoft 365 resources from outside the c
x: You need to enforce MFA for all users accessing Microsoft 365 resources from outside the corporate network. Which Conditional Access policy configuration achieves this with the least administrative effort? Option B is correct because it specifically targets external access using named locations (trusted locations), which is the standard and most efficient way to require MFA for non-corporate networks. Option A incorrectly uses risk-based conditions instead of location. Option C would require MFA everywhere including inside the office. Option D uses a block action instead of MFA requirement.

ti: SC-300: What is the primary difference between User risk and Sign-in risk detections in Microsoft
x: What is the primary difference between User risk and Sign-in risk detections in Microsoft Entra ID Protection? Option B is correct because User risk focuses on the likelihood an account is compromised (e.g., leaked credentials), whereas Sign-in risk evaluates the specific login attempt (e.g., anomalous location or impossible travel). Option A is incorrect as both can be real-time or offline. Option C is wrong because both can use similar remediation methods. Option D is incorrect as both apply to all identity types.

ti: SC-300: Contoso is piloting passwordless authentication. The security team wants to allow users to
x: Contoso is piloting passwordless authentication. The security team wants to allow users to sign in with FIDO2 security keys for Microsoft 365 but only from compliant devices. Which two configurations are required? (Choose two.) Option A is correct because the Authentication methods policy must explicitly enable FIDO2 keys before they can be used. Option C is also correct because authentication strengths allow Conditional Access policies to require specific methods like FIDO2. Option B is incorrect because there is no 'Passwordless sign-in' grant control. Option D is incorrect as there is no such tenant-wide setting.

ti: SC-300: Which of the following is a supported method for registering a FIDO2 security key in Micro
x: Which of the following is a supported method for registering a FIDO2 security key in Microsoft Entra ID? Option B is correct because users can register FIDO2 keys via the MySecurityInfo portal, during Windows setup, and through the Authenticator app. Option A is too restrictive. Option C is incorrect because FIDO2 and Windows Hello for Business are separate. Option D is incorrect because end users cannot register keys from the admin center.

ti: SC-300: A user reports they cannot complete MFA registration because they do not have a mobile pho
x: A user reports they cannot complete MFA registration because they do not have a mobile phone. The organization wants to allow this user to use Microsoft Authenticator on a tablet instead. What should you do? Option C is correct because the Authentication methods policy controls which methods (including Authenticator app) are available for users to register and use. Option A only controls persistent sessions. Option B does not enable the method. Option D would weaken security and is not best practice.

ti: SC-300: You are configuring a Conditional Access policy to require MFA for all administrators. The
x: You are configuring a Conditional Access policy to require MFA for all administrators. The policy should not apply when an administrator is accessing the Entra admin center from a hybrid Azure AD joined device in the corporate office. Which two conditions should you configure? (Choose two.) Option B is correct because targeting specific admin groups or roles is the recommended method. Option C is correct because excluding trusted corporate locations prevents MFA when admins are in the office. Option A is wrong because you should not include all users then exclude roles for admin-only policies. Option D is incorrect because excluding hybrid joined devices would likely increase MFA prompts.

ti: SC-300: What is the effect of setting a risk-based Conditional Access policy to 'Medium and above'
x: What is the effect of setting a risk-based Conditional Access policy to 'Medium and above' for Sign-in risk with a 'Block access' control? Option B is correct because selecting 'Medium and above' includes both medium and high risk sign-ins, and the 'Block' grant control prevents access. Option A is incorrect because low risk is excluded. Option C is incorrect because it ignores medium risk. Option D is wrong because the policy uses Block, not Require MFA.

ti: SC-300: Your organization wants to implement phishing-resistant MFA. Which authentication method s
x: Your organization wants to implement phishing-resistant MFA. Which authentication method should you recommend? Option C is correct because FIDO2 security keys are phishing-resistant as the private key never leaves the device and requires physical presence. Options A, B, and D can all be phished to varying degrees. Microsoft recommends FIDO2 or Windows Hello for Business for phishing-resistant authentication.

ti: SC-300: You notice several users have a 'User risk' state of 'At risk' in the Identity Protection
x: You notice several users have a 'User risk' state of 'At risk' in the Identity Protection dashboard. What is the recommended first step to remediate these users? Option B is correct because a risk-based Conditional Access policy is the recommended automated way to force password changes for users at risk. Option A is too disruptive. Option C is not possible because users at risk are typically blocked from self-service password reset. Option D is manual and not scalable for many users.

ti: SC-300: Which of the following cannot be used as a condition in a Microsoft Entra Conditional Acce
x: Which of the following cannot be used as a condition in a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy? Option D is correct because Conditional Access does not support 'days since last password change' as a condition. Options A, B, and C are all valid conditions: User risk is available when Identity Protection is enabled, browser can be filtered, and client app type is a standard condition.

ti: SC-300: You are the identity administrator for Contoso. The company wants to enforce MFA for all u
x: You are the identity administrator for Contoso. The company wants to enforce MFA for all users accessing Microsoft 365 resources from outside the corporate network. Which Conditional Access policy configuration achieves this with the least administrative effort? Option A is correct because it specifically targets external access using named locations (trusted locations) and applies only to Microsoft 365 apps, which is the most targeted and least disruptive approach. Option B is too broad as it would require MFA from inside the corporate network as well. Option C only targets guests and specific client apps, which does not meet the requirement. Option D relies on Identity Protection risk signals instead of location, which is not the requirement.

ti: SC-300: What is the primary difference between Security defaults and Conditional Access policies i
x: What is the primary difference between Security defaults and Conditional Access policies in Microsoft Entra ID? Security defaults provide a basic set of preconfigured security settings that cannot be modified, whereas Conditional Access policies offer granular, customizable control over when and how authentication is enforced. Both features are available with Azure AD Premium P1. Security defaults enable multiple security features including MFA for all users.

ti: SC-300: Your organization is piloting passwordless authentication using Microsoft Authenticator. A
x: Your organization is piloting passwordless authentication using Microsoft Authenticator. A pilot user reports they can no longer sign in after their phone was replaced. What is the most likely cause? Passwordless authentication using Microsoft Authenticator is tied to the specific device. When a user gets a new phone, they must re-register the new device as an authentication method. This is a common scenario during passwordless deployments. Options B, C, and D are not the primary cause of this specific issue.

ti: SC-300: Which of the following correctly describes how Microsoft Entra ID Identity Protection risk
x: Which of the following correctly describes how Microsoft Entra ID Identity Protection risk detections work? Identity Protection uses two main risk types: user risk (likelihood the account is compromised) and sign-in risk (likelihood the sign-in request is not from the account owner). These risk signals can be used in Conditional Access policies and are available with Microsoft Entra ID P2. Option C is incorrect because risk-based policies are commonly used with Conditional Access.

ti: SC-300: You need to implement MFA for a group of executives who frequently travel internationally.
x: You need to implement MFA for a group of executives who frequently travel internationally. The solution must minimize false positives while still providing strong security. Which Conditional Access configuration should you use? Using sign-in risk as a condition (option B) is the most intelligent approach as it leverages Identity Protection's machine learning to only challenge users when anomalous behavior is detected. This reduces friction for legitimate travel while still providing strong protection. Option A would create excessive MFA prompts during normal travel. Option C creates too much friction. Option D could inadvertently block legitimate travel.

ti: SC-300: What is the minimum license required to use risk-based Conditional Access policies that le
x: What is the minimum license required to use risk-based Conditional Access policies that leverage Identity Protection? Risk-based Conditional Access policies that use user risk and sign-in risk require Microsoft Entra ID P2 (formerly Azure AD Premium P2). Microsoft Entra ID P1 includes Conditional Access but not the Identity Protection risk analytics. Microsoft 365 E3 includes P1 capabilities but not P2.

ti: SC-300: Contoso is implementing phishing-resistant authentication. The security team wants to requ
x: Contoso is implementing phishing-resistant authentication. The security team wants to require Windows Hello for Business for all users accessing sensitive applications. Which policy type should be used to enforce this requirement? Authentication strength policies (a type of Conditional Access grant control) allow organizations to require specific strong authentication methods such as phishing-resistant methods like Windows Hello for Business or FIDO2 keys. This is the recommended modern approach for enforcing phishing-resistant authentication. The other options cannot enforce specific authentication methods at this granularity.

ti: SC-300: A user receives a Conditional Access prompt requiring MFA but their only registered authen
x: A user receives a Conditional Access prompt requiring MFA but their only registered authentication method is a phone number that no longer works. What is the recommended administrative action? A Temporary Access Pass (TAP) is the recommended secure method to allow a user to sign in and register new MFA methods when they have lost access to all their authentication methods. Option B would weaken security. Password reset (option C) would not help if they cannot complete MFA. Option D is unnecessary and disruptive.

ti: SC-300: Which of the following is a valid authentication method that can be used with passwordless
x: Which of the following is a valid authentication method that can be used with passwordless sign-in in Microsoft Entra ID? FIDO2 security keys are fully supported for passwordless sign-in and are phishing-resistant. SMS, security questions, and email OTP are not considered passwordless methods and do not meet modern passwordless requirements. Microsoft strongly recommends FIDO2 keys or Microsoft Authenticator for passwordless scenarios.

ti: SC-300: You are investigating a risky user flagged by Identity Protection. The user risk level is
x: You are investigating a risky user flagged by Identity Protection. The user risk level is listed as High and the detection type is 'Leaked credentials'. What is the recommended immediate action? When Identity Protection detects leaked credentials with a High risk level, the recommended action is to force a password change and re-register MFA methods. This mitigates the immediate risk of the compromised credentials being used. Simply monitoring (B) or permanently disabling (C) are not the best first responses. Excluding the user (D) would reduce security.

ti: SC-300: You are the identity administrator for Contoso. The company wants to enforce MFA for all u
x: You are the identity administrator for Contoso. The company wants to enforce MFA for all users accessing Microsoft 365 apps from outside the corporate network. Which Conditional Access policy configuration achieves this with the least administrative effort? Option A is correct because it specifically targets access from outside trusted locations for Microsoft 365 apps, meeting the requirement with precision. Option B incorrectly uses device state instead of location. Security defaults (C) would enforce broader MFA requirements that may exceed the stated need. Option D only handles registration, not enforcement during sign-in.

ti: SC-300: What is the primary difference between User Risk and Sign-in Risk detections in Microsoft
x: What is the primary difference between User Risk and Sign-in Risk detections in Microsoft Entra ID Protection? Option B is correct. User Risk assesses the likelihood an identity has been compromised (e.g., leaked credentials), whereas Sign-in Risk evaluates the legitimacy of a particular login attempt (e.g., anomalous location or impossible travel). The other options contain factual inaccuracies regarding timing, available controls, and licensing.

ti: SC-300: Contoso recently enabled passwordless authentication using Microsoft Authenticator. Some u
x: Contoso recently enabled passwordless authentication using Microsoft Authenticator. Some users report they can no longer sign in from their iOS devices. Which setting should you verify first? Option A is correct because the Authentication methods policy must explicitly enable passwordless phone sign-in for the Microsoft Authenticator app. The other choices, while potentially relevant in other scenarios, are not the primary reason passwordless sign-in would fail specifically on iOS devices after enabling the feature.

ti: SC-300: Which of the following is a supported method for registering a FIDO2 security key in Micro
x: Which of the following is a supported method for registering a FIDO2 security key in Microsoft Entra ID? Option B is correct. FIDO2 keys can be registered by users via My Security Info or during the OOBE for Microsoft Entra joined devices. Option A is too restrictive, C is incorrect because users can self-register, and D is false because the Authenticator app does not register FIDO2 keys.

ti: SC-300: You need to reduce the risk of MFA fatigue attacks against executives. Which Conditional A
x: You need to reduce the risk of MFA fatigue attacks against executives. Which Conditional Access policy setting should you configure? Option B is correct because requiring phishing-resistant authentication methods (such as FIDO2 or Windows Hello for Business) significantly mitigates MFA fatigue (also known as push bombing) attacks. The other options do not directly address the MFA fatigue vector.

ti: SC-300: What occurs when a user is added to the 'Users at high risk' risk-based Conditional Access
x: What occurs when a user is added to the 'Users at high risk' risk-based Conditional Access policy with a 'Block access' grant control? Option B is correct. Risk-based policies evaluate the risk level calculated by Identity Protection at the time of sign-in. If the user's risk is high, the block is enforced. Option A is incorrect because blocking is risk-based, not permanent. Options C and D misrepresent the policy behavior.

ti: SC-300: Your organization wants to implement number matching in Microsoft Authenticator to improve
x: Your organization wants to implement number matching in Microsoft Authenticator to improve MFA security. Which license is required to use this feature? Option C is correct. Number matching and additional advanced MFA features such as location context in the Authenticator app require Microsoft Entra ID P2 licensing. P1 and Free tiers do not support these enhanced MFA protections.

ti: SC-300: You notice several users have been flagged for 'Anonymous IP address' sign-in risk. What i
x: You notice several users have been flagged for 'Anonymous IP address' sign-in risk. What is the most likely cause? Option A is correct. The 'Anonymous IP address' detection typically indicates sign-ins from anonymous proxy services such as TOR. Option C relates to leaked credentials (User Risk), while B and D relate to other risk detections such as unfamiliar features or atypical travel.

ti: SC-300: Which of the following best describes the effect of enabling 'Require reauthentication eve
x: Which of the following best describes the effect of enabling 'Require reauthentication every 30 days' in a Conditional Access policy for Microsoft 365 applications? Option A is correct. The Sign-in frequency control in Conditional Access can require users to reauthenticate (password + MFA) at a specified interval. Option D is close but incorrect because the control applies regardless of activity. The other options are factually wrong.

ti: SC-300: A security audit reveals that several service accounts are using basic authentication to a
x: A security audit reveals that several service accounts are using basic authentication to access Exchange Online. What is the recommended approach to secure these accounts while maintaining functionality? Option B is correct. The long-term recommended solution is to move away from basic authentication entirely by adopting modern authentication with OAuth 2.0 using secrets or certificates. Blocking legacy auth (A) would break the service accounts. Options C and D do not solve the root problem.

ti: SC-300: Your organization needs to allow a third-party SaaS application to authenticate users via
x: Your organization needs to allow a third-party SaaS application to authenticate users via single sign-on without storing credentials. The solution must support both SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect. Which workload identity type should you create in Microsoft Entra ID? An app registration is required when you need to configure custom authentication settings, expose APIs, or support modern protocols such as OIDC and SAML for third-party applications. x: You need to grant a web application the ability to call the Microsoft Graph API as the signed-in user. The application uses OIDC for authentication. x: You need to ensure that all users who are members of the 'Finance-Approvers' group have their group membership reviewed every 90 days. What should you create in Microsoft Entra ID? x: You are configuring a Lifecycle Workflow to run when a user's 'employeeHireDate' attribute is within 5 days. Which workflow category and trigger type should you select? x: Contoso is implementing entitlement management. They want users to be able to request access to an access package that expires after 90 days unless renewed. x: Your organization wants to allow managers to request access packages on behalf of their direct reports. Which entitlement management setting must be enabled to support this scenario? x: A company is planning to use lifecycle workflows to automate the offboarding process.
